intro.title: Context Performance
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that demonstrates how to optimize performance when using React Context. You will learn to prevent unnecessary re-renders by splitting context providers and using memoization techniques like React.memo. The core concept involves understanding how context updates trigger re-renders in consuming components and how to control them. You will work with React's Context API, TypeScript for type safety, and functional components with hooks. By the end, you'll have a practical example showing performance improvements in a controlled scenario.
intro.usecase: React Context performance optimization is crucial in complex applications like e-commerce platforms where product filters, shopping cart states, and user preferences need to be shared across many components. In dashboard applications with multiple real-time data visualizations, poorly optimized context can cause sluggish updates across charts, tables, and status panels. Developers implementing multi-step forms or collaborative editing tools must ensure context updates don't trigger unnecessary re-renders of unrelated UI sections. This pattern is essential for maintaining smooth user interactions in applications with deeply nested component trees that share dynamic state.
